A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 21-page versions of the same AUTOSPEC paper. The main text, figures, algorithms, proofs, and Appendices A.1–A.5 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on 9-room and 100-room navigation and PandaGym manipulation, including learning curves, randomized-environment analyses, and computational costs.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix A.3, including the performance comparisons in Figures 4–11.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 and Algorithm 7 add the OrRefine update β(e_i) := β(e) ∩ β(e_i). V1 constrained the newly added edge but did not impose this intersection on the existing onward edge. This locally changes the safety constraints of the alternative path while retaining the four-procedure framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 9-room refinement scenarios, fixed and randomized 100-room navigation environments, and PandaGym manipulation task. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The DiRL and LSTS comparisons in Section 4 and the DiRL-based individual-refinement experiments in Appendix A.3 retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both retain the same PPO settings, network sizes, satisfaction threshold p = 0.99, 1000 evaluation rollouts, and best-path probability calculation. Environment-generation procedures and training timestep settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The individual-refinement tests, DiRL-versus-LSTS failure analysis, and randomized-environment bottleneck and corridor-switching analyses are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both specify five random seeds and learning curves reporting means with error bars described as mean ± variance. Runtime uncertainty reporting is also unchanged, with no added statistical tests or uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: The performance plots and numerical findings are unchanged. For example, both show approximately 60% AUTOSPEC versus 20% DiRL terminal success in Figure 6 and report approximately 240 seconds for the baseline versus 390 ± 42 seconds for AUTOSPEC. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds the safety-label intersection to the OrRefine proof, supplying a previously missing restriction on the existing onward edge. The theorem statement, mathematical definitions, other proof cases, and incompleteness argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: automated specification refinement, four soundness-preserving procedures, integration with existing specification-guided RL algorithms, and improved learning from coarse specifications.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 removes the explicit explanation that relaxing avoid regions can admit originally forbidden states and break soundness, although the underlying restriction remains in the formulas. The exploration-dependence interpretation and limitations concerning finite witnesses, incompleteness, and nonoptimal refinements are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 6 corrects its replacement edge from u* → u to u* → u′, aligning the detailed pseudocode with the method already described in v1's main text. Algorithm 7's edited notation still inconsistently inserts e_ui after defining e_new. Hyperparameters, hardware, environment-generation instructions, and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to existing specification-guided RL methods are unchanged. Bibliography differences concern page flow rather than citation membership.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits, shortens the AvoidRefine explanation, renames the new OrRefine edge, and replaces specific appendix references with generic references. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All eleven figures retain identical graphical content and captions. Text and figure placement reflow, including Figure 5 moving upward on page 10 and the conclusion fitting entirely on that page; Algorithm 7 also gains a wrapped line.

improvement.justification: The added OrRefine intersection addresses a concrete safety gap in v1's construction and proof, while Algorithm 6 now matches the intended target described in the main text. These localized corrections improve reliability despite Algorithm 7's remaining naming inconsistency and less precise appendix references. The empirical evidence and broader conclusions are unchanged.
